instructions: Classify the PRIMARY intent of this business email (Enron corpus): what the email's author wants the recipient to know or do. Forwards: when the newest message adds nothing of its own beyond a pointer (FYI, see below, a one-line comment), judge the forwarded content; when the newest message makes its own ask, notice or point, judge that. Tie-breaks: an explicit ask beats an update; a meeting ask is meeting_invite; a formal notice beats an update; use other only when no label fits.

criteria.payment_demand: Asks the recipient to pay, settle or cure an amount owed or a default.
criteria.notice: Formally informs of a fact, breach, termination, change or intention with contractual, legal or procedural effect, including operational notices to many parties (an outage, a capacity or nomination change, a notice to all interested parties).
criteria.analysis: Assesses options, risks, positions, terms, legislation or data; it reasons rather than reports. A memo that analyses stays analysis even if it also mentions a call.
criteria.request: Asks the recipient for information, a document, approval or an action (not a meeting), even when the ask sits inside a status report.
criteria.update: Reports status, progress, events or figures without an ask or formal notice.
criteria.meeting_invite: The main point is to propose, schedule, move, confirm or cancel a meeting or call (a revised call schedule counts); a passing mention of a call inside other content does not.
criteria.press_communication: A press release or public, media-facing statement, forwarded or not.
criteria.other: None of the above: personal notes, empty forwards, auto-replies, and marketing, newsletters or spam from outside vendors.
